answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. When a job is disputed, randomly selected peers check the evidence; a proven lie slashes the stake and rewards the reporters. Creating many identities then requires many tokens, while coordinating them risks losing capital, so cheap accounts alone cannot buy influence. An umber agent on a violet island still faces the same bond requirement: the cost follows each identity, not its name or location.
